name: EGFR → RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK
summary: The classical MAPK cascade: a growth factor activates a receptor tyrosine kinase, which switches on RAS and a three-tier kinase relay ending in ERK-driven gene expression and proliferation.
clinical: Hyperactivated in many cancers: EGFR mutations (lung), KRAS (pancreas, colon, lung), BRAF V600E (melanoma). Drugs: erlotinib/osimertinib (EGFR), sotorasib (KRAS G12C), vemurafenib/dabrafenib (BRAF), trametinib (MEK).

references.label: Lavoie, Gagnon & Therrien (2020) Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol 21:607 — ERK signalling review

nodes.label: EGFR
nodes.description: Dimerises and autophosphorylates on ligand binding.

edges.label: negative feedback
edges.description: ERK phosphorylates SOS, dampening further RAS activation.

steps.title: 1 · Ligand binding
steps.text: EGF binds the extracellular domain of EGFR, promoting receptor dimerisation.

steps.title: 2 · Autophosphorylation
steps.text: The kinase domains activate each other (asymmetric dimer) and phosphorylate tyrosines in the C-terminal tails. These pTyr residues are docking sites for the SH2 domain of GRB2.

steps.title: 3 · SOS activates RAS
steps.text: GRB2 brings the exchange factor SOS to the membrane, where it swaps GDP for GTP on RAS. RAS-GTP is the active switch.

steps.title: 4 · The kinase cascade
steps.text: RAS-GTP recruits RAF, which phosphorylates MEK, which dual-phosphorylates ERK on its TEY motif. Each tier amplifies the signal.

steps.title: 5 · Into the nucleus
steps.text: Active ERK enters the nucleus and phosphorylates transcription factors such as ELK1, inducing FOS and later cyclin D1.

steps.title: 6 · Proliferation and feedback
steps.text: Cyclin D1 drives G1 progression (see Cell-Cycle Regulation). ERK also phosphorylates SOS — a negative feedback loop that limits signal duration.
